historical_references.reference: Al-Bukhari records a tradition from Abu Hurairah about Zhabyun in his Sahih, Book 1, Number 61. According to this tradition, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said that a man from the Ansar named Zhabyun would intercede for the people of Hell on the Day of Judgment. The time period for this event is the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (610-632 CE).
historical_references.context: Prophetic tradition about intercession for people of Hell by a man named Zhabyun from Ansar.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Kathir in his Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah records that Zhabyun was a man from the Ansar and a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was known for his constant weeping for the sins of the Muslims. The context suggests that this was a pious man who showed deep concern for the wellbeing of his community. The time period for this event is also the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (610-632 CE).
historical_references.context: Biographical account of Zhabyun, a pious Ansari companion of the Prophet Muhammad known for his constant weeping for the sins of the Muslims.
